summary: This Docusaurus plugin generates an RSS 2.0 feed by scanning blog markdown files, extracting their HTML content from the built output, cleaning up unwanted UI elements, and assembling a feed with metadata like authors, images, and article content. It handles special cases like draft posts, normalizes URLs to be absolute, and manually injects author tags using custom XML manipulation since the underlying feed library doesn't support them natively.

explanations.62: path.posix.join uses forward slashes (/) even on Windows, ensuring URLs are consistent. We then add a leading slash if missing so paths always start with '/'.
explanations.78: We remove trailing slashes from the site URL, then concatenate it with the full path (which already has a leading slash from posixJoin) to create a complete URL like 'https://example.com/blog/my-post'.
explanations.87: We extract just the file extension (like '.png' or '.jpg') from the URL and convert it to lowercase so it matches our switch cases reliably.
explanations.113: We replace non-breaking spaces and zero-width spaces with regular spaces or nothing, then strip out control characters that would break XML parsers—these are invisible characters like backspace or null.
explanations.135: We combine critical selectors (like headers and SVGs that should always be removed) with default selectors and any user-provided selectors, so the final list includes all three categories.
explanations.154: We try to find an <article> tag first as the main content container, then fall back to Docusaurus theme-specific selectors if the article tag doesn't exist.
explanations.170: For each code snippet wrapper, we check if it contains the actual code block inside it. If so, we replace the wrapper with just the code block; otherwise we remove the entire wrapper.
explanations.189: If the slug is explicitly set in front matter, we normalize it by removing leading and trailing slashes, then return it or null if it's empty.
explanations.225: We dynamically import the Feed library here instead of at the top because the plugin needs context and options first. This is called inside postBuild when Docusaurus runs the build.
explanations.250: We read and parse the authors.yml file (if it exists) using js-yaml so we can look up author details by key later when building RSS items.
explanations.264: frontMatter() parses a markdown file into two parts: attributes (the YAML header) and body (the markdown content below the header).
explanations.270: We skip draft and unlisted posts because they don't generate HTML pages in the build output, so there's nothing to extract for the RSS feed.
explanations.274: If no explicit date is set in front matter, we use the file's birth time (creation time) as the post date.
explanations.292: filter(Boolean) removes all the null values from the array (posts we skipped due to being draft/unlisted/invalid), leaving only valid posts.
explanations.306: We spread (copy) all properties from item into a new object and add fullContentBody (the extracted HTML) as a new property.
explanations.312: We filter again to exclude posts marked published: false and posts with no HTML content, then sort by date newest first.
explanations.316: We take only the first maxItems posts (up to the limit), but Math.max(1, Number(maxItems)) ensures we get at least 1 item even if maxItems is 0 or invalid.
explanations.329: Instead of using the current time, we use the date of the newest post as the 'last updated' time for the feed—this prevents unnecessary redeployments if no articles actually changed.
explanations.335: authors can be a string, an array of strings, or undefined, so we normalize it to always be an array for consistent processing.
explanations.342: We look up each author key in the authorsData object, keep only those that exist, then extract just their name field.
explanations.364: We convert the relative image path from front matter to an absolute URL using the site URL and base URL, or null if no image is specified.
explanations.370: If images are enabled and we have an image URL, we prepend an tag to the description so it shows at the top of the RSS item.
explanations.396: The spread operator with a conditional object {...(condition && { key: value })} only adds the enclosure property to the item if all three conditions are true (images enabled, URL exists, MIME type found).
explanations.406: We store the custom dc:creator XML string in a temporary property so we can access it later when manually injecting it into the final XML.
explanations.422: cheerio.load with xmlMode: true parses the RSS string as XML instead of HTML, so it preserves namespaces and self-closing tags properly.
explanations.425: We add the Dublin Core namespace declaration to the root <rss> element so the dc:creator tags we inject are recognized as valid XML.
explanations.437: We iterate through the source posts by index, then match each one to the corresponding XML item at that same index (since feed generated them in order).
explanations.448: We retrieve the custom dc:creator XML string we stored earlier in the feed item's metadata.
explanations.457: append() adds the dc:creator XML string as a child element inside the <item> tag, so it appears in the final RSS output.
explanations.466: We replace the default XML declaration with our own version that also includes a stylesheet reference, so RSS readers and browsers can render the feed nicely.
